extra.label: IBIT structural positive: BlackRock cuts minimum in-kind conversion threshold 96% ($25M → $1M) — reduces friction for large Bitcoin holders entering the ETF structure
extra.value: BlackRock announced a 96% reduction in the minimum Bitcoin amount required for in-kind conversions into IBIT from $25 million to $1 million. The lower threshold makes it easier for large Bitcoin holders (family offices, hedge funds, high-net-worth individuals) to move coins directly into the IBIT structure without selling into cash first — reducing market impact and preserving the tax-advantaged structure. Long-term: this is a structural ETF demand catalyst that should expand IBIT's addressable market of potential in-kind contributors. Near-term: it does not reverse today's $144.67M net outflow, but it positions IBIT for stronger future inflows when market sentiment recovers. This is the most bullish structural development of the step-aside period.
